-- Format, sort, duplicates and legacy - SQL Server audit query
-- Exported from ATLAS Align on 2026-11-16. 19 enabled steps; disabled steps are left out.
-- Generated from Developer Logic. Review the code and test it on sample data before relying on the results.
--
-- Review:
--   - Step 6 overwrites [Worker ID], but the source columns are not listed in the audit. Replace SELECT * in that step with the column list so [Worker ID] is not selected twice.
--   - Step 7 overwrites [Worker ID], but the source columns are not listed in the audit. Replace SELECT * in that step with the column list so [Worker ID] is not selected twice.
--   - Step 8 overwrites [Worker ID], but the source columns are not listed in the audit. Replace SELECT * in that step with the column list so [Worker ID] is not selected twice.
--   - Step 9 overwrites [Worker ID], but the source columns are not listed in the audit. Replace SELECT * in that step with the column list so [Worker ID] is not selected twice.
--   - The audit does not list the columns of wd, sap, so those steps use SELECT *. Check for columns selected twice.
--
-- Source tables (replace these names if your tables are named differently):
--   - [WD_Workers]: wd
--   - [SAP_HI0256]: sap
--   - [wd]
--   - [sap]

WITH
-- Step 1: Reference wd
-- Reference source file "WD_Workers" as "wd":
step_1 AS (
  SELECT * FROM [WD_Workers] AS [wd]
),

-- Step 2: Reference sap
-- Reference source file "SAP_HI0256" as "sap":
step_2 AS (
  SELECT * FROM [SAP_HI0256] AS [sap]
),

-- Step 3: Reference Source
-- Reference source file "wd" as "wd":
step_3 AS (
  SELECT * FROM [wd] AS [wd]
),

-- Step 4: Join / Union Sources
-- Join file "wd" column "Worker ID" and file "sap" column "PERNR".
step_4 AS (
  SELECT [wd].*,
         [sap].*
  FROM step_3 AS [wd]
  LEFT JOIN [sap] AS [sap]
    ON [wd].[Worker ID] = [sap].[PERNR]
),

-- Step 5: Format Field
-- Format file "wd" column "Worker ID" as text.
step_5 AS (
  SELECT *, CAST(CAST(NULL AS NVARCHAR(4000)) AS NVARCHAR(4000)) AS [Worker ID]
  FROM step_4
),

-- Step 6: Format Field
-- Format file "wd" column "Worker ID" as number.
step_6 AS (
  SELECT *, TRY_CAST([Worker ID] AS DECIMAL(38, 10)) AS [Worker ID]
  FROM step_5
),

-- Step 7: Format Field
-- Format file "wd" column "Worker ID" as date MM/DD/YYYY.
step_7 AS (
  SELECT *, CONVERT(VARCHAR(10), TRY_CONVERT(date, [Worker ID]), 101) AS [Worker ID]
  FROM step_6
),

-- Step 8: Format Field
-- Format file "wd" column "Worker ID" as 8 digits with leading zeros.
step_8 AS (
  SELECT *, RIGHT(REPLICATE('0', 8) + CAST([Worker ID] AS VARCHAR(50)), 8) AS [Worker ID]
  FROM step_7
),

-- Step 9: Format Field
-- Format file "wd" column "Worker ID" as currency with two decimals.
-- Note: Format "currency with two decimals" is not a standard option. Check the formulas before running.
step_9 AS (
  SELECT *, FORMAT([Worker ID], 'currency with two decimals') AS [Worker ID]
  FROM step_8
),

-- Step 10: Sort Records
-- Sort records by file "wd" column "Hire Date" in Descending order.
-- The sort order is applied in the final SELECT (and to later Remove Duplicates steps).

-- Step 11: Sort Records
-- Sort records by file "wd" column "Country" in Ascending order, then by column "Pay" in Descending order.
-- The sort order is applied in the final SELECT (and to later Remove Duplicates steps).

-- Step 12: Remove Duplicates
-- Identify rows where all values match across these columns: file "wd" column "Worker ID" and column "Position", remove duplicates and keep the first record.
step_12_ranked AS (
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY [Worker ID], [Position] ORDER BY [Country] ASC, [Pay] DESC) AS [Duplicate Rank]
  FROM step_9
),

step_12 AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM step_12_ranked
  WHERE [Duplicate Rank] = 1
),

-- Step 13: Remove Duplicates
-- Identify rows where all values match across these columns: file "wd" column "Worker ID" and column "Position", remove duplicates and keep the last record.
step_13_ranked AS (
  SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY [Worker ID], [Position] ORDER BY [Country] ASC, [Pay] DESC) AS [Duplicate Rank], COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY [Worker ID], [Position]) AS [Duplicate Count]
  FROM step_12
),

step_13 AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM step_13_ranked
  WHERE [Duplicate Rank] = [Duplicate Count]
),

-- Step 14: Remove Duplicates
-- Identify rows where all values match across these columns: file "wd" column "Worker ID" and column "Position", remove duplicates and keep none of the duplicated records.
step_14_ranked AS (
  SELECT *, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY [Worker ID], [Position]) AS [Duplicate Count]
  FROM step_13
),

step_14 AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM step_14_ranked
  WHERE [Duplicate Count] = 1
),

-- Step 15: Split Field
-- Split file "wd" column "Legal Name" on the space and display part 1 in column "First Name".
step_15 AS (
  SELECT *, LEFT([Legal Name], CHARINDEX(' ', [Legal Name] + ' ') - 1) AS [First Name]
  FROM step_14
),

-- Step 16: Logic Step
-- IF file "wd" column "Status" is equal to "Active", THEN Keep matching rows.
-- Note: Display - Keep only rows that match this condition.
step_16 AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM step_15
  WHERE [Status] = 'Active'
),

-- Step 17: Logic Step
-- IF file "wd" column "Status" is not equal to "Active", THEN Exclude matching rows.
-- Note: Do Not Display - Keep only rows that do not match this condition.
step_17 AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM step_16
  WHERE NOT ([Status] <> 'Active')
),

-- Step 18: Logic Step
-- IF file "wd" column "Email" is blank/null, THEN display text response "Missing email" in column "Error Message".
step_18 AS (
  SELECT *, CASE WHEN NULLIF(LTRIM(RTRIM([Email])), '') IS NULL THEN CONCAT_WS('||', NULLIF(CAST(NULL AS NVARCHAR(4000)), ''), 'Missing email') ELSE CAST(NULL AS NVARCHAR(4000)) END AS [Error Message]
  FROM step_17
),

-- Step 19: Logic Step
-- IF file "wd" column "Status" is equal to "Terminated", THEN do NOT display record.
-- Note: Do Not Display - Keep only rows that do not match this condition.
step_19 AS (
  SELECT *
  FROM step_18
  WHERE NOT ([Status] = 'Terminated')
)

SELECT *
FROM step_19
ORDER BY [Country] ASC, [Pay] DESC;
pythonScript:
# Format, sort, duplicates and legacy - Python (pandas) audit script
# Exported from ATLAS Align on 2026-11-16. 19 enabled steps; disabled steps are left out.
# Generated from Developer Logic. Review the code and test it on sample data before relying on the results.
#
# Before running: fill in SOURCE_PATHS and OUTPUT_PATH below.
# Requires pandas and numpy, plus openpyxl to read or write Excel files.

import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Required variables: set these paths before running
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Source files to read, one per source the audit uses (.csv, .txt, .xlsx, .xls).
SOURCE_PATHS = {
    "wd": "",
    "sap": "",
}

# File to write the audit results to (.csv or .xlsx).
OUTPUT_PATH = ""

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Reading and writing files
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
EXCEL_EXTENSIONS = {".xlsx", ".xlsm", ".xls"}
TEXT_EXTENSIONS = {".csv", ".txt"}


def check_paths():
    """Stops with a message when a required path is blank or a file is missing."""
    blank = [f"SOURCE_PATHS[{name!r}]" for name, path in SOURCE_PATHS.items() if not path]
    if not OUTPUT_PATH:
        blank.append("OUTPUT_PATH")
    if blank:
        sys.exit("Set these paths at the top of the script: " + ", ".join(blank))
    missing = [path for path in SOURCE_PATHS.values() if not Path(path).is_file()]
    if missing:
        sys.exit("These source files were not found: " + ", ".join(missing))


def read_source(path):
    """Reads a source file, choosing the reader from its extension."""
    extension = Path(path).suffix.lower()
    if extension in EXCEL_EXTENSIONS:
        return pd.read_excel(path)
    if extension in TEXT_EXTENSIONS:
        return pd.read_csv(path)
    sys.exit(f"{path}: use a .csv, .txt, .xlsx or .xls file.")


def write_output(df, path):
    """Writes the results, choosing the writer from the file extension."""
    extension = Path(path).suffix.lower()
    if extension in EXCEL_EXTENSIONS:
        df.to_excel(path, index=False)
    elif extension in TEXT_EXTENSIONS:
        df.to_csv(path, index=False)
    else:
        sys.exit(f"{path}: OUTPUT_PATH must end in .csv or .xlsx.")


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Audit logic
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
def run_audit(sources):
    """Runs the audit steps in order and returns the results."""
    # Step 1: Reference wd
    # Reference source file "WD_Workers" as "wd":
    df = sources["wd"].copy()

    # Step 2: Reference sap
    # Reference source file "SAP_HI0256" as "sap":
    df = sources["sap"].copy()

    # Step 3: Reference Source
    # Reference source file "wd" as "wd":
    df = sources["wd"].copy()

    # Step 4: Join / Union Sources
    # Join file "wd" column "Worker ID" and file "sap" column "PERNR".
    df = df.merge(sources["sap"], how="left", left_on="Worker ID", right_on="PERNR", suffixes=("", "_sap"))

    # Step 5: Format Field
    # Format file "wd" column "Worker ID" as text.
    df["Worker ID"] = df["Worker ID"].astype("string")

    # Step 6: Format Field
    # Format file "wd" column "Worker ID" as number.
    df["Worker ID"] = pd.to_numeric(df["Worker ID"], errors="coerce")

    # Step 7: Format Field
    # Format file "wd" column "Worker ID" as date MM/DD/YYYY.
    df["Worker ID"] = pd.to_datetime(df["Worker ID"], errors="coerce").dt.strftime("%m/%d/%Y")

    # Step 8: Format Field
    # Format file "wd" column "Worker ID" as 8 digits with leading zeros.
    df["Worker ID"] = df["Worker ID"].astype("string").str.zfill(8)

    # Step 9: Format Field
    # Format file "wd" column "Worker ID" as currency with two decimals.
    # Note: Format "currency with two decimals" is not a standard option. Check the formulas before running.
    df["Worker ID"] = df["Worker ID"].astype("string")

    # Step 10: Sort Records
    # Sort records by file "wd" column "Hire Date" in Descending order.
    df = df.sort_values(["Hire Date"], ascending=[False], kind="stable")

    # Step 11: Sort Records
    # Sort records by file "wd" column "Country" in Ascending order, then by column "Pay" in Descending order.
    df = df.sort_values(["Country", "Pay"], ascending=[True, False], kind="stable")

    # Step 12: Remove Duplicates
    # Identify rows where all values match across these columns: file "wd" column "Worker ID" and column "Position", remove duplicates and keep the first record.
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=["Worker ID", "Position"], keep="first")

    # Step 13: Remove Duplicates
    # Identify rows where all values match across these columns: file "wd" column "Worker ID" and column "Position", remove duplicates and keep the last record.
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=["Worker ID", "Position"], keep="last")

    # Step 14: Remove Duplicates
    # Identify rows where all values match across these columns: file "wd" column "Worker ID" and column "Position", remove duplicates and keep none of the duplicated records.
    df = df.drop_duplicates(subset=["Worker ID", "Position"], keep=False)

    # Step 15: Split Field
    # Split file "wd" column "Legal Name" on the space and display part 1 in column "First Name".
    df["First Name"] = df["Legal Name"].astype("string").str.split(" ", regex=False).str[0]

    # Step 16: Logic Step
    # IF file "wd" column "Status" is equal to "Active", THEN Keep matching rows.
    # Note: Display - Keep only rows that match this condition.
    mask = df["Status"] == "Active"
    df = df[mask]

    # Step 17: Logic Step
    # IF file "wd" column "Status" is not equal to "Active", THEN Exclude matching rows.
    # Note: Do Not Display - Keep only rows that do not match this condition.
    mask = df["Status"] != "Active"
    df = df[~mask]

    # Step 18: Logic Step
    # IF file "wd" column "Email" is blank/null, THEN display text response "Missing email" in column "Error Message".
    mask = df["Email"].fillna("").astype(str).str.strip().eq("")
    df["Error Message"] = df.get("Error Message", "")
    existing = df.loc[mask, "Error Message"].fillna("").astype(str)
    df.loc[mask, "Error Message"] = existing.where(existing == "", existing + "||") + "Missing email"

    # Step 19: Logic Step
    # IF file "wd" column "Status" is equal to "Terminated", THEN do NOT display record.
    # Note: Do Not Display - Keep only rows that do not match this condition.
    mask = df["Status"] == "Terminated"
    df = df[~mask]

    return df


def main():
    check_paths()
    sources = {name: read_source(path) for name, path in SOURCE_PATHS.items()}
    results = run_audit(sources)
    write_output(results, OUTPUT_PATH)
    print(f"Wrote {len(results):,} rows to {OUTPUT_PATH}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
